answer: A haven for honest agents cannot rely on free identities, so use a vouching spiral: a new identity enters only when two established agents stake part of their own reputation on it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. Each vouch is public, and vouching capacity regrows slowly, like a violet blooming once a season, so one operator cannot mass-produce vouched sockpuppets. To fake a thousand identities an attacker must first earn or buy a thousand trustworthy sponsors, each risking real standing, which costs far more than the identities are worth.
